'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
****[[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian President]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] says that [[Ukraine]] is open to continue peace talks with [[Russia]] if they guarantee the restoration of preinvasion borders, return the [[Ukrainians]] who were forcefully evacuated to [[Russia]], and if [[Russian Ground Forces|Russian troops]] withdraw from the country. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/volodymyr-zelensky-olaf-scholz-boris-johnson-moscow-russia-b2073304.html?amp (''The Independent'')] [https://www.axios.com/2022/05/07/zelensky-demands-ukraine-russia-peace-talks (Axios)]
***Ukrainian MP [[Oleksiy Goncharenko]] claims that the Russian frigate ''[[Russian frigate Admiral Makarov|Admiral Makarov]]'' was struck with [[R-360 Neptune|Neptune anti-ship missiles]] off of [[Snake Island (Ukraine)|Snake Island]]. Russia denies having any information of the strike. [https://www.newsweek.com/russia-ukraine-peskov-admiral-makarov-black-sea-ship-1704189 (''Newsweek'')]
*[[Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso]]
**Eleven people are killed and nine others are injured in [[Islamist]] attacks in [[Loroum Province|Loroum]] and [[Sanmatenga Province|Sanmatenga]] provinces, [[Burkina Faso]]. Twenty attackers are also killed. [https://apnews.com/article/islamic-state-group-ouagadougou-business-west-africa-ea31bc9f3f34f5a848efb86f5693eafc (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Acquisition of Twitter by Elon Musk]]
**The Orlando Police Pension Fund files a [[Class action#United States 2|class-action lawsuit]] in the [[Delaware Chancery Court]] against [[Twitter Inc]] and [[Elon Musk]], seeking to delay the acquisition of Twitter to 2025. [https://www.reuters.com/business/musk-twitter-are-sued-by-shareholder-over-44-bln-takeover-2022-05-06/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Hotel Saratoga explosion]]
**At least 26 people are killed and at least 74 others are injured by an explosion caused by a suspected gas leak at the [[Hotel Saratoga, Havana|Hotel Saratoga]] in [[Havana]], [[Cuba]]. [https://apnews.com/article/explosions-cuba-caribbean-havana-5b8057c9a85c63521ca5306dd86e1567 (AP)]
*Two people die and over 100 more are rescued as a boat carrying migrants runs aground in southern [[Italy]]. [https://apnews.com/article/europe-migration-italy-e03bcb016142f17bc244c6ebd638dccb (AP)]
*Two people are killed and eighteen others are injured when an [[explosion]] occurs in a residential building in [[Madrid]], [[Spain]]. [https://apnews.com/article/europe-explosions-madrid-5e09280351fae6ec9450f048e612b0d0 (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in Colombia]]
***[[Colombia]] announces that it will offer a second [[COVID-19 vaccine]] [[booster dose|boosters]] for people aged above 50 years. It comes after the country reached its target for fully vaccinate 70% of population. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/colombia-offer-second-coronavirus-booster-shots-over-50s-others-2022-05-06/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
***[[China]] decides to making regular [[COVID-19 testing]] mandatory for its citizens with setting up thousands of permanent [[Polymerase chain reaction|PCR]] testing stations, with 9,000 already completed in [[Shanghai]] alone, as authorities aim to "normalise" tough pandemic controls even after the current round of [[COVID-19 lockdowns in China|lockdown]]s end. [https://www.livemint.com/news/world/china-plans-to-make-regular-covid-19-testing-part-of-residents-lives-read-here-11651831838140.html (''Livemint'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan]]
***[[Taiwan]] reports a record 30,035 new [[COVID-19]] cases in the past 24 hours, which is the first time the country has reported more than 30,000 cases since the pandemic began. [https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/4528503 (Taiwan News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Iran–Sweden relations]]
**[[Iran]] detains a Swedish man who was travelling as a tourist, allegedly in response to [[Sweden]] [[Trial of Hamid Nouri|prosecuting Hamid Nouri]], an Iranian official considered to be responsible for the [[1988 executions of Iranian political prisoners|mass killings of political prisoners in 1988]]. [https://apnews.com/article/europe-middle-east-iran-arrests-tehran-becea0e61053e169b2983ba4b3cfd459 (AP)]
*[[Iran–United States relations]]
**The [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] passes 62–33 a non-binding resolution barring the [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] from removing the [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] from its [[United States Department of State list of Foreign Terrorist Organizations|list of Foreign Terrorist Organizations]]. [https://www.haaretz.com/us-news/.premium-u-s-senate-passes-non-binding-motion-barring-biden-from-moving-irgc-off-terror-list-1.10781145 (''Haaretz'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*Two people are killed and three others are injured during a [[mass shooting]] at a care home in Molensingel, [[Alblasserdam]], [[Netherlands]]. The perpetrator was already wanted for murdering a man at a shop yesterday. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-61347237 (BBC News)]
*Sofia Sapega, the girlfriend of Belarusian activist [[Roman Protasevich]], with whom she was detained when [[Ryanair Flight 4978|their flight]] was diverted by the [[Belarusian Air Force]] last year, is sentenced to six years in prison for "inciting social hatred". The exiled [[Belarusian opposition]] condemns the verdict. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/belarus-hands-six-year-jail-sentence-dissidents-girlfriend-after-forced-plane-2022-05-06/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2022 Sri Lankan protests]]
**The [[Sri Lankan government]] declares a [[state of emergency]] in response to massive anti-government protests. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/anti-government-protest-strike-sri-lanka-shuts-schools-businesses-2022-05-06/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2022 NHL Entry Draft]]
**[[NHL commissioner]] [[Gary Bettman]] says that Russian players will remain eligible for the upcoming [[NHL Entry Draft|NHL Draft]] despite other clubs [[Boycott of Russia and Belarus|banning]] Russian athletes. [https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/bettman-says-russian-players-can-be-picked-in-2022-nhl-draft/ (Sportsnet)]
